quote: within 240 days (i.e. eight (8) months) of the day UCSF Medical Center sends the first bill
explanation: The policy sets a 240 day window to apply and only extends it for good cause. California law does not allow any time limit on applying.
The policy asks for checking and savings statements and says missing requested information can be grounds for denial. California law does not let hospitals consider your savings.

quote: no later than 180 days following the date of the first post-discharge statement
explanation: The policy says you must apply within 180 days of the first statement. California law does not allow a time limit on applying.

quote: Assets include, but are not limited to, cash, checking accounts, saving accounts, stocks, bonds
explanation: The policy lists savings and investments as assets and only exempts part of them, so the rest are counted. California law does not let hospitals count your savings.

quote: The first $10,000 of monetary assets and 50% of monetary assets over the first $10,000.
explanation: Only part of your savings is exempt, so the rest is counted toward eligibility. California law does not let hospitals count your savings at all.

quote: Prime authorizes vendors following regulations to report to the credit bureau(s) no sooner than 150 days
explanation: The policy lets collectors report debts to credit bureaus and does not exclude California patients. California law now bans credit reporting of hospital debt.

quote: A patient may provide a completed Financial Assistance Application, including all requested supporting documentation, at any time.
explanation: This California policy says you can apply at any time. The 240 day window is a federal tax rule period, not a cutoff for applying.
The eligibility worksheet has a line for your total savings. Nothing says it is only for Medicare waivers, so savings appear to be counted, which California law forbids.

quote: The Payment Assistance application form requests specific information regarding Qualified Monetary Assets.
explanation: The application asks for your cash and savings to decide help. California law does not let hospitals consider your savings.

quote: CommonSpirit Hospital Organizations may accept documentation of assets but shall not require it.
explanation: The California addendum controls this policy. It limits asset use to Medicare cost sharing and health savings accounts, which the law allows.

quote: Return your completed application along with all supporting documentation within 30 days of receipt of the application.
explanation: The form tells you to return the application within 30 days. California law does not allow any time limit on applying.
The charity application asks for your savings, trust accounts and total assets plus a bank statement. California law does not let hospitals consider your savings.
The eligibility worksheet has a line for your total savings. Nothing says it is only for Medicare waivers, so savings appear to be counted, which California law forbids.

quote: All patients must apply for Medi-Cal before charity care funds are considered.
explanation: The letter says you must apply for Medi-Cal before getting charity care. California law lets hospitals require only a Medi-Cal screening, not an application.
The application asks for your checking, savings and other account balances. California law does not let hospitals consider your savings.

quote: Signed waiver or release from the patient or the patient’s family, authorizing the hospital to obtain account information
explanation: The policy asks for bank statements and a release to check the value of your savings. California law does not let hospitals consider your savings.
